title: The optimal asymptotic rate of binary error-correcting codes
decision_reason: Explicit published problem, independent current specialist corroboration, full relevant claim-scope comparisons, duplicate screening and separated A43 self-review passed.

problem_fingerprint.objects: All binary codes C subset {0,1}^n, without a linearity restriction; Hamming distance counts differing coordinates.
problem_fingerprint.model: A_2(n,d) is the largest code cardinality for which every distinct pair has Hamming distance at least d.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For each fixed real delta in (0,1/2), let n tend to infinity and determine R_2(delta) throughout that interval.
problem_fingerprint.conclusion: Determine the exact optimal asymptotic rate function, rather than only improve an upper or lower bound.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Binary alphabet; logarithm base 2; fixed delta before the limsup; integer distance rounded up, following Alrabiah-Guruswami 2026 and Barg 2026.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Existential, unrestricted codes. No efficient construction/encoding/decoding requirement. Not stochastic Shannon capacity, list decoding, quantum codes, fixed finite blocklength, or an entry restricted to linear/LDPC/constant-weight codes.

independent_corroboration.assessment: AG26 has no authors in common with CJJ22 and explicitly treats the optimal unrestricted rate as undetermined, alongside its own improved bounds. Barg gives a separately authored subsequent specialist account.
independent_corroboration.limitation: GJL26 shares an author with CJJ22 and is not counted as independent of it. The late-published LL26 text retains an obsolete upper-bound description. Scholarly corroboration does not mean independent review of this draft.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: General linear and nonlinear binary codes; variational upper bounds under a cq-channel error condition.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Stronger upper bounds without a matching achievability theorem. Quantum channels are a proof device; the bounded codes remain classical.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Further asymptotic upper bounds and a monotone Horn–channel hierarchy.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: No equality with the unrestricted optimal rate is asserted; §1 explicitly retains the exponential gap.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: For fixed n,d, exact recovery at anchor order t at least A_2(n,d); full finite-completeness proof read.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: A finite optimization hierarchy does not evaluate its asymptotic exponent. The statement does not claim a fixed order determines R_2.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: R_2(delta) bounded above by a combined moving-projection exponent, below the second MRRW bound.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: An upper-bound improvement, with no matching lower bound. Do not admit 'improve MRRW' as a separate open question.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Polynomial factors improve finite code-cardinality/existence estimates at fixed relative distance.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Taking log_2 and dividing by n makes these gains O(log n/n). This rate-scope conclusion is an inference from the stated bounds, not a claim the finite improvements are trivial.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Claims Gilbert–Varshamov asymptotic tightness for linear subspaces; proof not adjudicated.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Even if valid, this does not upper-bound all nonlinear codes without a separate linear-optimality theorem. The original candidate was already unrestricted; no convenient new restriction was invented to evade the claim.

resolution_scope_comparisons.source: CJJ22 Theorem 1 and Proposition 2; CJJ23 Theorems 1.2–1.3; CJJLL26 Theorem 5.1
resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Finite completeness for linear-code hierarchies; CJJ22's unrestricted hierarchy collapses to Delsarte.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: No evaluation of the exact general asymptotic rate. LPs here are theoretical coding bounds, not numerical-linear-algebra questions.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Rate-half binary linear codes and duals approach their GV distances with efficient encoders.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Achieves a benchmark with extra algorithmic structure; does not prove optimality among all codes.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: TAG constructions and a conditional limitation of one curve-bound approach.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: No improved general existential exponent or optimality theorem is claimed. Technical curve theorem was not relied on.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Elementary proof of the historical first MRRW upper bound.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Re-proves an upper bound; no exact rate theorem. Its dated superlative is superseded by the August papers.

duplicate_review.method: Established full baseline and source/exclusion-map inventory, current full-text searches for Hamming/Gilbert/Varshamov/rate-distance/code aliases, all current titles, and rereading nearest statements.

nearest.difference: Stochastic deletions with unreported positions and average vanishing decoding error.
Strong powers of one fixed seven-symbol confusability graph, not growing binary Hamming-distance thresholds.
Computational recovery from random noisy parity samples, not codebook cardinality.
Sample complexity for reconstructing one string from deletion traces, not packing codewords.
Online weighted independent-set selection; unrelated information model and target.

duplicate_review.canonical_family: One unrestricted binary asymptotic rate function. No separate counts for GV tightness, linear codes, subintervals, finite blocklengths or efficient constructions.
